176: 
177: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |

180: | Dependency | The template contract keeps the required and optional anchor lists | The drift guard reports false drift | The guard calls the contract, so it inherits any change instead of hard-coding a list |
181: | Risk | A lane edits a file another lane owns | Two writers on one file | The three lanes own disjoint paths and the conductor checks `git status` after each lane |
182: | Risk | The fill text is too long for a table cell and breaks the template | A scaffold renders broken | Every line is one physical line and the fill test renders all 16 documents |

190: 
191: ### Performance
192: - **NFR-P01**: The 16 renders in the fill test finish under 60 seconds on the build worktree.
193: 
194: ### Security
195: - **NFR-S01**: No brief carries a credential, token or key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
196: 
197: ### Reliability
198: - **NFR-R01**: The drift guard is read-only and exits 1 on any drift, so a second run on the same tree prints the same lines.

202: ## 8. EDGE CASES
203: 
204: ### Data Boundaries
205: - Empty input: a template with no `## ` heading fails the fill test with a named message rather than passing silently.
206: - Maximum length: a fill line that would exceed 400 characters is shortened at authoring time. The test does not enforce a length, the review does.
207: 
208: ### Error Scenarios
209: - External service failure: a provider error stops the lane dispatch. The conductor records it and retries once after 10 minutes, then stops the phase.
210: - Phase 003 not closed: the token form is absent, but the heading locator still works. The conductor records the deviation and continues with the heading form.
211: - A section that exists only at one level: the fill line sits inside the same gate as the heading, so it renders only at that level.

20: ## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
21: 
22: Phase 003 turns every core hint into a value token. A token still does not tell a weak model what to write. This phase puts one imperative instruction below every section heading, with a good and a weak example, so the model copies a standard instead of inventing one. It also aligns the 14 drifted examples a model imitates and adds two guards so the guidance cannot rot.
23: 
24: **Key Decisions**: the guidance is an HTML comment below the heading, and the example drift guard delegates anchor comparison to the template contract.
25: 
26: **Critical Dependencies**: phase 003 must be closed, because every locator is written in both the pre-token and post-token form.

74: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
75: 
76: ### Problem Statement
77: A fresh Level 2 scaffold holds 97 bracketed hints and validates clean. A weak model leaves many of them in place, or replaces them with a sentence that restates the heading. The template says what field to fill but never what a good answer looks like. The 21 hand-written examples that a model imitates have drifted from the templates, so the model copies a skeleton the validator no longer expects.
78: 
79: ### Purpose
80: Every section tells a weak model the one action to take and shows one good and one weak answer. The examples match the templates again, and two commands fail when either property breaks.
81: <!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->

90: ### The fill line format (frozen)
91: 
92: One physical line, placed immediately below the section heading.
93: 
94: ```text
95: <!-- FILL: <instruction> GOOD: <good example> WEAK: <weak example> -->
96: ```
97: 
98: When the table below has `-` in both the Good and the Weak cell, the line is:
99: 
100: ```text
101: <!-- FILL: <instruction> -->
102: ```
103: 
104: Rules for the text inside the line:
105: - The instruction is one imperative sentence and ends with a period.
106: - No cell contains `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:`, `[NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:`, `-->`, `;` or an em dash. A short priority mark such as `[P0]` is allowed because it is not a token.
107: - The line is never wrapped. It is one line in the template source.
108: - The good example is concrete and short. The weak example is the failure a weak model produces: vague, generic or a restatement of the heading.
109: - The model deletes the line when it fills the section. A line left behind is not a placeholder, so it never fails the gate.

816: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
817: 
818: ### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading
819: 
820: **Status**: Accepted
821: 
822: **Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.
823: 
824: **Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing value tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.
825: 
826: **Consequences**:
827: - The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
828: - The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
829: - A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.
830: 
831: **Alternatives Rejected**:
832: - Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
833: - On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
834: - A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.
835: 
836: ### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint
837: 
838: **Status**: Accepted
839: 
840: **Context**: The four core templates hold 214 hints after phase 003 and 70 section rows across the four levels. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.
841: 
842: **Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.
843: 
844: **Consequences**:
845: - The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
846: - A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.
847: 
848: **Alternatives Rejected**:
849: - Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.
850: 
851: ### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract
852: 
853: **Status**: Accepted
854: 
855: **Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.
856: 
857: **Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.
858: 
859: **Consequences**:
860: - The guard and the validator read one source of truth.

# 1. CONFIGURATION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

readonly ORCHESTRATOR_JS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js"
readonly ORCHESTRATOR_TS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../lib/validation/orchestrator.ts"
readonly TSX_LOADER="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs"
readonly DIST_FRESHNESS_CJS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/dist-freshness.cjs"

readonly VERSION="3.0.0"

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. STATE & GLOBALS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

FOLDER_PATH=""
JSON_MODE=false STRICT_MODE=false VERBOSE=false QUIET_MODE=false
RECURSIVE=false RECURSIVE_OPT_OUT=false
CHILD_MANIFEST_ACTIVE=false CHILD_MANIFEST_HASH="" CHILD_MANIFEST_ENTRIES=() PHASE_DIRS=()

    [[ -f "$VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON" ]] || { echo "RULES: registry unavailable at $VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON"; return 0; }
    node -e '
const fs = require("fs");
const parsed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"));
const rules = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : (parsed.rules || []);
const lines = ["RULES BY CATEGORY:"];
const categories = [...new Set(rules.map((item) => item.category))];
for (const category of categories) {
  lines.push(`  ${category}:`);
  for (const rule of rules.filter((item) => item.category === category)) {
    const suffix = rule.strict_only ? " strict-only" : "";
    lines.push(`    ${rule.rule_id} [${rule.severity}${suffix}] - ${rule.description}`);
  }
}
process.stdout.write(`${lines.join("\n")}\n`);
' "$VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON" 2>/dev/null || echo "RULES: registry unreadable"
}

show_help() {
    cat << EOF
validate.sh - Spec Folder Validation (v$VERSION)

USAGE: ./validate.sh <folder-path> [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    --help, -h     Show help     --version, -v  Show version
    --json         JSON output   --strict       Run strict-only rules
    --verbose      Detailed      --quiet, -q    Results only
    --recursive    Validate parent + all [0-9][0-9][0-9]-*/ child phase folders
    --no-recursive Disable auto-recursive validation when phase children exist

ENVIRONMENT:
    SPECKIT_RULES              Comma-separated subset of rules to evaluate
    SPECKIT_SKIP_VALIDATION    1, true, yes or on skips validation (also read from hook-flags.env)
    SPECKIT_STRICT/_VERBOSE/_JSON/_QUIET   Equivalent to the flags above

EXIT CODES: 0=pass, 1=user error, 2=validation error, 3=system error

$(list_registry_rules)

### Frozen definitions

**Hint.** A bracketed text that matches `\[[A-Za-z/][^]\[]{2,}\]`. The slash lets the score cells `[/25]`, `[/20]` and `[/15]` count. Phase 1 counted with a letter-only start, so on the same Level 2 scaffold it saw 97 occurrences and this regex sees 101.

**Conversion rule.** The script `convert_hints.py` turns a hint into `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ` followed by the hint text and `]`. The text keeps its case. It skips five cases:
1. A line inside a fenced code block.
2. Text inside an inline code span.
3. Text followed directly by `(`, which is a link.
4. The five scaffolder texts `NAME`, `Feature Name`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `###-feature-name` and `1/2/3/3+`, and any text that starts with `template:`. `create.sh` replaces or strips them, so a token there would stay in every scaffold.
5. A text that already starts with `YOUR_VALUE_HERE`.

**Counts the conversion must give.** Converted per file: `spec.md.tmpl` 96, `plan.md.tmpl` 90, `tasks.md.tmpl` 7, `implementation-summary.md.tmpl` 11, `acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl` 10, so 214 in all. The total hint count of each file does not change, because a token is itself a hint under this regex. The bare hints left are exactly the ones in `tasks.md` T011.

**Stamp.** The 7 stamp lines of those five templates change from `| v2.2 -->` to `| v2.3 -->`: 3 in `spec.md.tmpl` and 1 each in the other four. The five manifest entries change the same way.

**Gate stamp.** A doc carries the gate stamp when one of its first 70 lines matches `<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: <names> | vMAJOR.MINOR -->` with MAJOR above 2, or MAJOR 2 and MINOR 3 or more. A doc with an older stamp or none does not.

**Lifecycle.**

| Doc | Status in `spec.md` | Unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` token | `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` | Strict result |
|-----|---------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|
| Gate stamp | Draft | warning | error | passes when nothing else errors |
| Gate stamp | any other value or none | error | error | fails |
| No gate stamp | any value | error | error | fails, as before |

Draft means the cell holds the word Draft, ignoring case, bold marks, backticks, outer quotes, trailing punctuation and repeated spaces. The first Status row of the metadata table counts.

### Key Components
- **`convert_hints.py`**: the conversion tool, saved by `tasks.md` T004.
- **`replace_block.py`**: replaces the lines from a start marker up to an end marker, and refuses unless each marker occurs once. Used for the orchestrator.
- **`mutate.py`**: replaces one exact text that must occur once. Used for the mutation checks.
- **`apply_edits.py`**: applies old-text and new-text pairs to a doc, and refuses unless each old text occurs once.
- **`strict-census.mjs`**: validates every folder in a list with the orchestrator built in this checkout and prints one row per folder.
- **`suite_compare.py`**: compares two suite outputs and allows only the new test file and its tests.
- **`placeholder-token-gate.vitest.ts`**: the new test.
- **Conductor**: runs every task and reads every output.
- **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` review at phase close.

# usage: convert_hints.py <template file>
# Rewrites the file in place and prints how many hints it turned into value tokens.
import re, sys

# A bracketed hint: a letter or slash, then at least two more characters, no nested brackets.
HINT = re.compile(r"\[(?!YOUR_VALUE_HERE)([A-Za-z/][^\]\[]{2,})\](?!\()")
# Text that create.sh replaces or strips at scaffold time must stay as written.
KEEP = ("NAME", "Feature Name", "YYYY-MM-DD", "###-feature-name", "1/2/3/3+")
CODE_SPAN = re.compile(r"`[^`]*`")

def convert_line(line):
    spans = [(m.start(), m.end()) for m in CODE_SPAN.finditer(line)]
    def inside_code(pos):
        return any(a <= pos < b for a, b in spans)
    def repl(m):
        body = m.group(1)
        if inside_code(m.start()) or body in KEEP or body.startswith("template:"):
            return m.group(0)
        counts["converted"] += 1
        return "[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: " + body + "]"
    return HINT.sub(repl, line)

path = sys.argv[1]
counts = {"converted": 0}
out, in_fence = [], False
for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n"):
    if re.match(r"^\s*(```|~~~)", line):
        in_fence = not in_fence
        out.append(line)
        continue
    out.append(line if in_fence else convert_line(line))
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out))
print(f"converted {counts['converted']} in {path}")
PY

 Every fact below came from a read-only command or a file read. The command is repeated so the conductor can confirm it on the post-003 tree.
 
 | Fact | Evidence |
 |------|----------|
-| The Level 1 anchor lists are exactly the six to seven names in the phase brief | A read of the four core templates gives spec `metadata problem scope requirements success-criteria risks questions`, plan the seven plan names, tasks the six tasks names and implementation-summary the six summary names |
+| The Level 1 anchor lists are exactly the six to seven names in the phase brief | `tasks.md` T003 renders each core template with `inline-gate-renderer.sh --level <level>`, extracts the names with `rg -o '<!-- ANCHOR:[a-z0-9-]+'` and saves the 16 sorted lists to `scratch/baseline/anchor-lists.txt`; the Level 1 lists are the six to seven names in the phase brief |
 | The renderer consumes only gate markers, and passes an ordinary HTML comment through to the output | `runtime/cli/templates/inline-gate-renderer.ts` lines 172 to 229: `GATE_OPEN`, `GATE_CLOSE` and `GATE_EMPTY` are the only comment shapes removed |
 | The validator gate scans an HTML comment for token syntax | `runtime/cli/rules/check-placeholders.sh` lines 59 to 97 filters fenced blocks only, then greps `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` and `[NEEDS_CLARIFICATION:` |
 | The standalone broad scan is `runtime/cli/spec/check-placeholders.sh`, not the rules file | `rules/check-placeholders.sh` defines `run_check` and has no main, so running it directly prints nothing and exits 0 |
 | `create.sh` replaces five hard placeholders and strips the provenance token | `runtime/cli/spec/create.sh` lines 965 to 984 replace the feature name, the date, the packet pointer and the level, and strip the template provenance token |
